device.category: 10-voice virtual analogue synthesizer module (2U rack or desktop), two parts, with voice modulator (vocoder), arpeggiator, RPS phrase player and motion control
device.based_on: The JP-8000 keyboard's analogue modelling engine (1996) in a module, released 1998; adds the Voice Modulator, external input synthesis, unison, distortion and 10-voice polyphony. Contains the JP-8000's 64 preset performances and 128 preset patches.

sources.title: Roland JP-8080 Owner's Manual (English, JP-8080_e3)
sources.note: Panel guide, every sound parameter, performance functions, arpeggiator, RPS, motion control, Voice Modulator, edit-menu parameters, memory, initialise values, parameter lists, transmit/receive table, Voice Modulator initialise table, MIDI implementation (v1.00, April 1998), chart and specifications. Blue Voice Modulator panel legends read from the front panel drawing on page 12.

architecture.synthesis_note: Virtual analogue: DSP models of analogue oscillators, filter and amplifier, plus four DSP waveforms with no analogue equivalent (super saw, triangle mod, feedback osc, filtered noise on OSC 1).
architecture.polyphony_mode: 10 voices (8 with the Voice Modulator on), newest note priority. Per patch: poly, MONO, LEGATO, UNISON or legato unison. Per performance: SINGLE, DUAL or SPLIT key mode, with Voice Assign splitting the voices between the parts in DUAL and SPLIT.
architecture.patch_memory_note: Two tiers. A patch is one sound (128 user, 384 preset in 3 groups of A/B banks of 64). A performance (64 user, 192 preset) holds complete copies of its Upper and Lower patches plus part, key mode, arpeggiator/RPS and Voice Modulator settings, so editing a stored patch does not change performances that used it. Edits go to a temporary area and must be written. RPS patterns (48), motions (2 sets of 2) and system settings are written directly. SmartMedia cards hold up to 64 x 64 performances and 128 x 64 patches.
architecture.summary: Per voice: OSC 1 offers seven waveforms, each with two waveform-specific CONTROL knobs; OSC 2 offers square, saw, triangle or noise (controls only for square and noise) or external audio, with RANGE, FINE/WIDE, SYNC to OSC 1 and RING modulation. OSC 2 can cross modulate OSC 1's frequency. An AD pitch envelope and LFO 1 act on both oscillators, OSC 2 only, or the cross mod depth. OSC BALANCE mixes the two into a 12/24 dB HPF, BPF or LPF with key follow, ADSR envelope and LFO 1; then the amp with ADSR, level and LFO 1 as tremolo, auto pan or manual pan. LFO 2 (triangle) is brought in by the mod wheel on pitch, filter and amp. Each patch has its own tone control, 13-type multi-effects and 5-type delay. Two parts play two patches; a Voice Modulator can turn them, external inputs or a robot oscillator into a vocoded or filter-banked signal. Velocity, aftertouch/breath (Control Up/Down), the voice (vocal morph) and recorded motions can each move almost every knob at once by preset widths.

modules.name: MIDI input and voice assigner
modules.description: There is no keyboard. Notes arrive at MIDI IN (on each Part MIDI channel) or REMOTE KBD IN (treated like the panel). The assigner gives Upper and Lower parts their voices per KEY MODE and Voice Assign, handles MONO/LEGATO/UNISON, and turns velocity, mod wheel, bend, aftertouch and breath into control signals. In Preview the BANK and NUMBER buttons play C4 to C5 at velocity 80.

properties.steal: newest note priority, oldest note released

modules.name: Pitch processing
modules.description: Sums note pitch, portamento, OSC SHIFT, part transpose, part detune, bend, unison detune and master tune into the pitch both oscillators follow.

modules.name: Oscillator 1
modules.description: Seven waveforms, each with its own meaning for CONTROL 1 and CONTROL 2 (see properties). Receives cross modulation from OSC 2 on its frequency, except with super saw or noise.

super_saw.control1: DETUNE: spread of the detuned saws
super_saw.control2: MIX: level of the detuned saws against the centre one

triangle_mod.control1: OFFSET: how far the triangle is reshaped; more overtones, little fundamental (like a high-passed square)

noise.control1: CUTOFF FREQ of a low-pass on noise; also raises level; tracks the key
noise.control2: RESONANCE; at 127 a sine (CUTOFF 64 = played pitch, one step per semitone)

feedback_osc.control2: FEEDBACK AMOUNT: level of the harmonics
feedback_osc.note: Guitar-feedback tone; forces MONO or LEGATO and blocks UNISON

saw.control1: SHAPE: strong fundamental at either end, thin (high-passed) at centre

modules.name: Oscillator 2
modules.description: Square (PWM), saw, triangle or noise, pitched relative to OSC 1 by RANGE and FINE/WIDE. Hard sync to OSC 1 (not with noise or EXT). With EXT on the waveform is replaced by external audio, gated by note-on and GATE THRESHOLD and not pitched.

noise.control1: CUTOFF FREQ (does not track the key)
noise.control2: RESONANCE; at 127 a sine (CUTOFF 64 = C4 on every key)

ext.control1: GATE THRESHOLD: minimum input level let through

modules.name: Ring modulator
modules.description: Multiplies OSC 1 by OSC 2; the result replaces OSC 2's output in the mix, so it is heard as OSC BALANCE moves towards OSC 2.

modules.name: Oscillator balance
modules.description: Crossfades OSC 1 and the OSC 2 path (OSC 2, ring or external input); equal at centre.

modules.name: Pitch envelope
modules.description: Attack-decay envelope to pitch or cross mod depth, chosen by LFO 1 & ENV DESTINATION; bipolar DEPTH.

modules.name: Filter
modules.description: Multimode HPF, BPF or LPF at -12 or -24 dB/octave, resonant to self-oscillation, with key follow.

modules.name: Filter envelope
modules.description: ADSR to cutoff with bipolar DEPTH; release time follows note-off velocity when assigned.

modules.name: Amplifier
modules.description: Patch level, amp envelope, LFO 1 as tremolo, auto pan or manual pan position.

modules.name: Amp envelope
modules.description: ADSR to the amplifier; release time follows note-off velocity when assigned. With Env Type in Solo = ANALOG a new note continues from the current level.

modules.name: LFO 1
modules.description: Triangle, saw, square or sample and hold, with FADE (time to full depth after key-on). Depth is set where it is used: OSC COMMON, FILTER, AMP and the OSC 1/OSC 2 CONTROL 2 knobs. Rate can follow tempo (LFO Sync).

modules.name: LFO 2 (MODULATION)
modules.description: Triangle LFO with its own rate, applied to pitch, filter and amp at three separate depths, scaled by the mod wheel (CC 1) of the controlling keyboard.

modules.name: Tone control
modules.description: Bass and treble shelving boost/cut on the patch output.

modules.name: Multi-effects
modules.description: One of 13 types (super chorus x4, flanger x3, deep phasing, jet phasing, twisting, freeze phase x2, distortion) at MULTI-FX LEVEL. Chorus rate can follow tempo or LFO 1 (Chorus Sync).

modules.name: Delay
modules.description: Five types (panning L>R, R>L, short; mono short, long) with TIME, FEEDBACK and LEVEL. Time can follow tempo (Delay Sync).

modules.name: External inputs
modules.description: INST/LOWER and VOCAL/UPPER line inputs and the front MIC input (through the mic amp, chosen by REAR/FRONT), each with a level knob and a limiter. INST/LOWER feeds the Lower part's OSC 2 and the Voice Modulator's Inst Input; VOCAL/UPPER or MIC feeds the Upper part's OSC 2 and the Vocal Input. With only INST/LOWER plugged (REAR), it feeds both parts.

modules.name: Morphing and motion
modules.description: Adds offsets to almost every patch knob and slider at once. Velocity Assign and Control Assign store a width of change per parameter in the patch; Control Up (aftertouch by default) moves each parameter by its width and Control Down (breath) by the mirror image. Vocal morph control and motion playback add their own changes. Overlapping sources sum, except that Control Assign and vocal morph take the last message received.

modules.name: Arpeggiator
modules.description: UP, DOWN, UP&DOWN or RANDOM over 1 to 4 octaves with 90 beat patterns, at TEMPO or MIDI clock. Driven only from REMOTE KBD IN or Preview; its notes go to MIDI OUT.

modules.name: RPS (Realtime Phrase Sequence)
modules.description: 48 one-key patterns on C#2 to C6, each up to 4 measures of 4/4 at 24 ticks per quarter, up to 10 notes at once; loop-mix recording with quantise and gate time.

modules.name: Motion control
modules.description: Records and plays back knob and slider moves (or controllers from REMOTE KBD IN) on the part chosen by PANEL SELECT: two sets (A, B) of two motions, loops of 1 to 8 measures or one pass up to 99.

modules.name: Voice Modulator Inst Input
modules.description: Sums what the formant filter imposes the voice on: the part output (VOICE MOD SEND), INST/LOWER (Ext->Inst Send), the robot oscillator and noise.

modules.name: Robot oscillator
modules.description: Internal carrier so the formant filter talks with no instrument input; ROBOT PITCH and ROBOT CONTROL (thick to intelligible).

modules.name: Voice Modulator noise
modules.description: Noise through a high-pass (V NOISE CUTOFF) mixed into the Inst Input for husky voices.

modules.name: Voice Modulator (formant filter / filter bank)
modules.description: Two identical sets of 12 band-pass filters. Formant filter (SOLID, SMOOTH, WIDE): the Vocal Input is analysed band by band and the detected levels shape the Inst Input in the same bands, with consonants (VOCAL MIX) added back, CHARACTER 1-12 band levels, RESONANCE, RELEASE, GATE THRESHOLD and VOCAL HOLD. Filter bank (FLT BANK WIDE, NARROW): both sets are 12-band graphic level controls, Inst Input left and Vocal Input right.

algorithms.wide: formant: wider bands, for non-voice modulators
algorithms.flt_bank_narrow: filter bank: narrow bands, AM radio

modules.name: Vocal morph detector
modules.description: Measures the Vocal Input around 1.2 kHz (so the vowel 'a' controls most) above a threshold and sends it as the Control Up or Control Down message by the sign of the sensitivity.

modules.name: Voice Modulator ensemble
modules.description: Ensemble, chorus, flanger or phaser types dedicated to the Voice Modulator output, deeper than the multi-effects chorus.

modules.name: Voice Modulator delay
modules.description: Delay dedicated to the Voice Modulator output, same five types and limits as the patch delay.

modules.name: Output
modules.description: Mixes both parts and the Voice Modulator to L and R (MIX OUT), or Lower to L and Upper to R (PARALLEL OUT); headphones carry the same; VOLUME LEVEL is not stored.

behaviours.name: Signal path
behaviours.rule: Per voice: OSC 1 and the OSC 2 path (OSC 2, ring or external input) through OSC BALANCE, filter, amp. All voices of a part then pass that patch's tone control, multi-effect and delay. The two parts, and the Voice Modulator, mix at the outputs.

behaviours.name: Two parts, one voice pool
behaviours.rule: A performance always holds an Upper and a Lower patch, each with its own effects. SINGLE plays the PANEL SELECT part; DUAL layers both (Part Detune spreads them); SPLIT puts Lower below the split point and Upper from it. In DUAL and SPLIT, Voice Assign fixes each part's share of the 10 voices (8 with the Voice Modulator on). New notes steal the oldest. On MIDI IN each part answers its own Part MIDI channel.

behaviours.name: Waveform-dependent controls
behaviours.rule: CONTROL 1 and 2 change meaning with the waveform (see module properties); the display names the parameter as you turn. OSC 2 saw and triangle have no controls; with EXT on, CONTROL 1 is the gate threshold. Noise with RESONANCE at 127 becomes a sine: on OSC 1 CUTOFF 64 gives the played pitch, on OSC 2 it gives C4 on every key; each step is a semitone.

behaviours.name: Feedback osc forces mono
behaviours.rule: Selecting FEEDBACK OSC turns MONO or LEGATO on, locks it on, and blocks UNISON.

behaviours.name: Sync, ring and cross mod
behaviours.rule: Sync resets OSC 2 at each OSC 1 cycle (not with noise or EXT); the tone changes with RANGE or FINE/WIDE while the pitch stays. Ring multiplies OSC 1 by OSC 2 and appears on the OSC 2 side of the balance. X-MOD lets OSC 2 frequency-modulate OSC 1 (not super saw or noise); sweep OSC 2 pitch for timbre changes. With LFO 1 & ENV DESTINATION on X-MOD the pitch envelope and LFO 1 move the cross mod depth: a positive envelope works best with low X-MOD DEPTH, a negative one with high.

behaviours.name: Centre-zero depths
behaviours.rule: Envelope and LFO depths are bipolar: centre is none, below or left inverts. Velocity, Control Assign and vocal morph move these depths only away from zero on the side the control sits; they cannot cross zero.

behaviours.name: Filter key follow
behaviours.rule: Centre fixes the cutoff; +32 tracks fully (100 %, equal brightness, also for HPF and BPF); +63 about 200 %; -64 about -100 %. Most audible with CUTOFF at centre.

behaviours.name: Amp pan modes
behaviours.rule: PAN off: AMP LFO 1 DEPTH is tremolo. AUTO: LFO 1 pans (FADE ignored). MANUAL: the knob sets a fixed position. Pan and panning delays are lost with a mono output or PARALLEL OUT.

behaviours.name: LFO 2 on the mod wheel
behaviours.rule: LFO 2 is a triangle with one rate and three stored depths (pitch, filter, amp); DEPTH SELECT only picks which depth the knob edits. Nothing is heard until CC 1 arrives; CC 1 resets on a performance change but not a patch change.

behaviours.name: Solo modes
behaviours.rule: MONO re-attacks every note; LEGATO glides overlapping notes without re-attack; UNISON stacks the part's voices with Unison Detune up to 50 cents; LEGATO+UNISON together give legato unison. Env Type in Solo ANALOG continues envelopes from their current level. Patch Gain compensates the lower level of mono patches.

behaviours.name: Velocity morphing
behaviours.rule: Set the sound for velocity 80, press VELOCITY ASSIGN, move controls to the velocity-127 sound, then return them. Each parameter then moves by its width above 80 and by the mirror below 80, relative to the current knob position. Filter and amp R follow note-off velocity, everything else note-on. Excluded: VOLUME, TEMPO, Voice Modulator CONTROL 1/2, input levels and the Voice Modulator panel.

behaviours.name: Control assign (aftertouch and breath)
behaviours.rule: Set the sound for no controller, press CONTROL ASSIGN, move controls to the full-aftertouch sound, return them. Control Up 0-127 adds the width; Control Down adds its mirror, so one gesture can push a sound two ways (the JP-8000 ribbon sends aftertouch on its right, breath on its left). With Morph Bend Assign the pitch follows by the bend ranges (REMOTE KBD IN only). Control Up/Down can be any CC 1-31, 33-95 or aftertouch.

behaviours.name: Motion control
behaviours.rule: Record knob and slider moves in loops (1-8 measures, layered pass by pass) or one pass of up to 99 measures; moving a recorded control overwrites it. Playback applies to the PANEL SELECT part. Turning a knob during playback takes over once it passes one of its 11 switch points, until the motion loops. Stopping a motion leaves the sound changed; reselect the patch to restore it. Motion Restart can restart it with the first key, aligning it with a pattern.

behaviours.name: Summing of morph sources
behaviours.rule: Velocity, Control Assign, vocal morph and motion offsets add on overlapping parameters, except Control Assign and vocal morph, which share the same messages: the last one received sets the value. morph.out stands for an offset onto every assigned parameter.

behaviours.name: Which part the controllers move
behaviours.rule: From REMOTE KBD IN: SINGLE and SPLIT act on the PANEL SELECT part, DUAL on both. From MIDI IN: the part whose Part MIDI channel matches the message.

behaviours.name: Arpeggiator and RPS
behaviours.rule: Driven only from REMOTE KBD IN or Preview. SINGLE: the PANEL SELECT part; DUAL: per Arpeggio Dest (arpeggio) or both parts (RPS); SPLIT: Lower only. RPS assigns a 1-4 measure pattern to each key C#2-C6, recorded by loop-mix with quantise and gate time; Pattern Trig Qtz times switching; HOLD keeps playing; keys outside the range stop a held pattern. Results go out on MIDI OUT. Lower needs enough voices for the pattern's chords.

behaviours.name: Tempo sync and halving
behaviours.rule: Chorus, delay, LFO 1, ensemble and Voice Modulator delay can follow TEMPO or MIDI clock (per MIDI Sync). Delays never exceed 1250 ms mono or 625 ms panning; a longer synced time is halved, repeating at half the interval.

behaviours.name: Formant filter
behaviours.rule: Needs both an instrument (part via VOICE MOD SEND, INST/LOWER via Ext->Inst, or the robot oscillator) and a voice (VOCAL/UPPER or MIC via Ext->Vocal). 12 bands of the voice set the levels of the same 12 bands of the instrument. Sustained, bright sounds work best; percussion as the modulator also works (WIDE). GATE THRESHOLD closes it under a level; VOCAL HOLD freezes it. Parameters marked formant-only show 'x' and are ignored in filter-bank algorithms.

behaviours.name: Filter bank
behaviours.rule: FLT BANK WIDE/NARROW make both sets 12-band level controls (CHARACTER 1-12) for stereo use: Inst Input left, Vocal Input right; VOICE MOD SEND feeds both; V PAN balances them. VOCAL HOLD is forced off.

behaviours.name: Vocal morph control
behaviours.rule: The Vocal Input's level around 1.2 kHz above Vocal Morph Thrsh becomes the Control Up (sensitivity +) or Control Down (-) message, moving the patch by its Control Assign widths. 'a' controls most; alternating vowels gives large and small changes. Does not need VOICE MOD SEND.

behaviours.name: Voice Modulator initialise
behaviours.rule: Nine set-ups write recommended performance values: F.FLT VINTAGE, SILKY, HUSKYVOICE, BREAKBEATS, ROBOT, HUSKYROBOT; F.BANK STANDARD, RADIO; VOCAL MORPH CTRL. INIT PERFORMANCE uses F.FLT VINTAGE.

behaviours.name: External input synthesis
behaviours.rule: With EXT on, the part's input replaces OSC 2: heard only during note-on and above GATE THRESHOLD, at the filter and amp, without pitch. Set OSC BALANCE fully to OSC 2 to hear only the input. INST/LOWER goes to Lower; VOCAL/UPPER or MIC to Upper; INST/LOWER alone (REAR) to both.

behaviours.name: Individual and external trigger
behaviours.rule: Held notes wait for a trigger to start the filter and/or amp envelope: a note on Indv Trig Src CH (MIDI IN, SINGLE or DUAL) or below the split point (REMOTE KBD IN, SPLIT, Upper only), or the part's external input crossing GATE THRESHOLD (attack on rising, release on falling). Without triggers those envelopes do not run.

behaviours.name: Memory and editing
behaviours.rule: Selecting a performance or patch loads it into the temporary area; edits mark '*' and are lost on reselection unless written. Patches inside performances are copies. MANUAL (SHIFT) sets the part's patch to the physical knob positions. Temporary and Edit Scope show values; Velocity and Control Scope show widths.

behaviours.name: Panel MIDI
behaviours.rule: With Tx/Rx Edit on, MODE1 sends each knob as the CC in its access list, or SysEx where none is assigned; MODE2 lets each knob use any CC 1-31, 33-95, aftertouch or SysEx (non-standard). Both ends must use the same mode. VOLUME, TEMPO, Voice Modulator CONTROL 1/2, input levels and the Voice Modulator panel are never sent.

source_inconsistencies: OSC SHIFT is described as 'set independently for each performance' (p.71), but it sits in the patch section of the panel and in the Patch Parameters list (p.182); modelled as a patch parameter.
The RPS range is C#2 (note 37) to C6 (note 84) on p.92 and p.95, but the HOLD text on p.92 gives C#2 as note 36.
OSC 2 RANGE detents are listed as '24, -12, 0, +12 and +24' (p.69); -24 is presumably meant.
RPN 0 accepts 0-24 semitones (00H-18H) but the same entry says up to one octave can be set (p.192).
Ensemble Type lists FLANGER SLOW/DEEP/FAST in the parameter list (p.185) but only FLANGER SLOW and FAST in the Voice Modulator chapter (p.110); modelled with all three.
Dimensions are printed as 482 (W) x 88 (D) x 264 (H) mm; for a 2U rack unit 88 mm is the height and 264 mm the depth.
The LFO 2 and Bend Range pages (pp.87, 89) tell you to 'erase the control assign settings of the other Patch' to limit them to one part, apparently copied from the Control Assign page.

p.11 says motions can record 'nearly all' sliders and knobs 'for up to 99 measures, in four separate memories'; p.210 gives 99 measures as the recording length and 8 as the loop length, consistent only if 99 is the play-once mode.

modelling_gaps.detail: The schema has no per-part scope. One patch's voice architecture is modelled; at run time the Upper and Lower parts each run it with their own patch and their own tone control, multi-effect and delay (scope 'common' here means once per part). Part assignment of the external inputs is folded into ext.to_osc2.

Schema memory values are patch, global or none. Performance-level settings are marked memory 'patch' with the note 'Stored in the performance, not the patch.' A 'performance' value (schema 0.14.0) would make this explicit.

Velocity Assign and Control Assign are per-parameter width tables stored in the patch, not slot-based routings, so they are not a mod_matrix. They are modelled as the morph module, two width parameters and behaviours b11-b14; morph.out is wired to cutoff only as a representative.

Eighteen knobs and sliders also edit Voice Modulator parameters on the Voice Modulator panel. These are separate parameters whose access notes name the physical control (read from the blue legends on p.12).
Super saw (seven detuned saws), triangle mod, feedback osc and filtered noise are described only by their sound. A model needs measurements or the JP-8000's later documentation.
No times, rates or frequencies are given; all panel parameters are 0-127 or -64 to +63 as stored.
Access lists record MODE1 and the MODE2 factory CCs; user MODE2 reassignment is a global table not enumerated.
Preset performance and patch names are not included; the lists are in the manual (pp.176-181) if wanted.
